Report of the Academic Calendar Committee (ACC) Abraham Kovoor, Chair February 23, 2023 Faculty Senate Meeting The ACC presented its initial report at the October 20, 2022 Senate meeting and as a result, three bills were approved and signed. This legislation addressed: Juneteenth as a holiday in the summer calendar; the Wednesday before Thanksgiving as a non-standard day; and adjustments to the Columbus Day/Indigenous People’s Day holiday in the long-range calendar. The initial report also addressed a question related to commencement. Given the growing size of the student body and the number of programs offered, the University has space limitations for various graduation-related events. This has led to scheduling such events over the course of a full weekend and this should be reflected in the Calendar. There was no objection to this proposal when originally presented last October but formal approval is now requested. A seconded motion from the ACC now comes to the Faculty Senate: “That the University adopt and the calendar reflect the addition of the Friday immediately previous to the Commencement Weekend (formally just Saturday and Sunday) for Commencement Activities and that the Faculty Senate confirm the change in the calendar for transparency.”

CONSTITUTION, BY-LAWS, AND UNIVERSITY MANUAL COMMITTEEReport #2022-2023-16 -MOTIONFACULTY SENATE, February 23, 2023 Context and rationale: Request from Enrollment Services Advisory Council (ESAC) to the FacultySenate Executive Committee (FSEC), referred directly by FSEC to CBUM to create a policy for resolvinggrades of incomplete within a timely manner and that would trigger the assignment of an automaticpermanent grade when the student or instructor does not meet the grade change deadline.
CBUMreviewed and discussed the ESAC proposal, and considered recommendations from the Curriculumand Standards Committee, the Teaching, Advising and Assessment Committee, the Faculty SenateExecutive Committee, and the Office of the Provost.

CBUM proposes to the Faculty Senate amendments to our current policy to: ● clarify the temporary nature of the grade of Incomplete and the unique and infrequentcircumstances in which it is appropriate to assign the grade of Incomplete, ● encourage student and faculty accountability in the process of resolving Incompletes, ● promote efficient and just resolution of Incompletes to convert these temporary grades intopermanent grades by the time the student graduates, and ● trigger an automatic grade change to a non-punitive “NC” when the instructor does notsubmit a grade change report prior to the student’s official graduation date.
Current language in Chapter 8 - Academic Regulations: 8.53.20 Incomplete.
A student shall receive a report of “Incomplete” in any course in which the course workhas been passing up until the time of a documented precipitating incident or condition, but has not beencompleted because of illness or another reason which in the opinion of the instructor justifies the report.

Aninstructor who issues a grade of “Incomplete” may forward a written explanation to the student’s academicdean. #15-16-30 8.53.21 The student receiving an “Incomplete” shall make necessary arrangements with the instructor or, in theinstructor’s absence, with the instructor’s chairperson to remove the deficiency.
This arrangement shall bemade prior to the following mid semester for the undergraduate student and within one calendar year for thegraduate student.
Proposed changes and additions to Chapter 8 - Academic Regulations: 8.53.20 Incomplete.
A student shall receive a temporary grade report of “Incomplete” in any course in whichthe when course work has been passing up until the time of a but is not completed by the end of the semesterdue to documented precipitating incident or condition, but has not been completed because of extenuatingcircumstances beyond the ability of the student to predict and control, such as a serious illness or medicalcondition, or another compelling reason which in the opinion of the instructor justifies the grade.

An instructorwho issues a grade of “Incomplete” may forward a written explanation to the student’s academic dean.Assignment of the temporary grade of Incomplete is made sparingly and presumes both that the studentintends and will be able to complete the coursework in the established time frame, and that the instructorintends and will be able to review the completed work in that established time frame. #15-16-30

8.53.21 Resolution of Grades of Incomplete.
The student receiving an “Incomplete” shall make necessaryarrangements with the instructor to remove the deficiency. or, iIn the instructor’s absence, with theappropriate administrator shall manage the process of resolving grades of Incomplete (the instructor’schairperson in the case of programs with a chairperson, and in the case of programs without a chairperson, theinstructor’s college dean or the designee of the instructor’s college dean).
This arrangement shall be madeprior to the submission of the temporary grade of Incomplete whenever possible, and not later than prior tothe following mid semester for the undergraduate student and within one calendar year for the graduatestudent.
This arrangement shall not include plans for the student to officially re-enroll in the course during afuture term: official re-enrollment accompanied by a grade reported on a future grade roster shall not resolvethe temporary grade of Incomplete (see 8.53.23).

This arrangement shall include a deadline for completion ofmissing work to which both the student and the instructor (or, in the instructor’s absence, the appropriateadministrator) have consented in writing. 8.53.22 Deadline for Submission of Incomplete Work.
The final deadline to complete and submit missing workto resolve the temporary grade of Incomplete and thus seize the opportunity to earn a permanent letter gradeis the date stipulated in writing in the arrangements made by the student with the instructor or, in theinstructor’s absence, with the appropriate administrator (see 8.53.21).
Such date shall be not later than the lastday of classes of the last semester in which the student enrolls in degree applicable coursework.
If the studentdoes not submit the incomplete work by the stipulated deadline, the instructor retains the right to submit agrade change report to replace the temporary grade of Incomplete with a permanent letter grade reflectingboth the submitted and unsubmitted work. 8.53.23 Grade Change Report for Grades of Incomplete and Deadline for Grade Changes.

The sole manner bywhich a temporary grade of Incomplete shall be changed to a permanent letter grade with a quality point valueis through submission of the change of grade form by the instructor or, in the instructor’s absence, theappropriate administrator.
The grade change from the temporary grade of Incomplete to a permanent lettergrade as a result of a special examination or the completion of other work shall be reported by the instructoror, in the instructor’s absence, the appropriate administrator (see 8.53.21), via the change of grade form to theOffice of Enrollment Services within 72 hours of such examination or completion (see 8.56.11), unless the examis taken and/or the work is submitted during the final exam period of a semester or term, in which case thegrade change shall be reported by the deadline for grade submission for that semester or term, as listed in theUniversity academic calendar. 8.53.24 Final Resolution of Grades of Incomplete.
Permanent letter grades submitted via the change of gradeform shall replace the temporary grade of Incomplete (“I”) on the transcript.

A grade of Incomplete that is notresolved through the report of a grade change by the student’s official date of graduation shall result in a gradechange to the permanent, non-punitive grade of “NC” (not completed).
Grade changes for grades receivedbefore graduation will not be permitted after graduation unless the change is based on clerical or proceduralerrors and the change is received and posted to the student’s record by the last day of classes of the semesterfollowing the term in which the student graduates (see 8.56.12).

The September 2021 Hanover report on micro-credentials identified “Business, Management, Marketing, and Related Services” as the top credentialing area.
Recent research on the future of digital and social marketing highlighted its variety of opportunities and benefits and its inherent challenges.
Specific expertise is required to navigate this space.
Drawing from the Occupational Outlook Handbook from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the following are examples of application of the skills from this certificate.
Many of these roles require a bachelor’s degree for entry.
While the BLS does not specify social media in the titles, digital and social media is a core part of many marketing and promotional plans and demand for expertise is increasing.

For individuals whose bachelor’s degree is not in marketing or similar fields, a post-baccalaureate certificate like this provides the specialized knowledge required for entry into the fields.
The data on attainment level for these roles has split between bachelors and masters level degrees, implying education beyond a bachelors is valued.
Our regional competition would be Southern New Hampshire University's Social Media Certificate that focuses heavily on marketing topics and is similar to content offered by Hubspot.
Another potential competitor could be the Northeastern University's Social Media for Organizational Performance but their focus is on marketing fundamental and strategy implementation, is more expensive and takes longer to complete.
Our program is unique because it focuses exclusively on social media and how to use it strategically and includes a course on content creation which is not offered by any of our potential competitors.
Also, we will allow the students access to social media content management system, so they can learn to collect and analyze data in real-time, rather than working with secondary data.

At the completion of the certificate, each student will have a well-researched and field-tested social media campaign that can be implemented at a real company.

However, despite the numerous advantages of social media use for business and public relations, many organizations are unaware of how they can use social media to maximize the benefits of social media marketing and communication.
Many practitioners are unaware of the need for communication strategies to enhance their sales and reputations.
As the world of social media rapidly changes and grows, having an effective social media communication strategy is imperative.
Using a theory-driven and evidence-based approach, participants will learn how to develop effective social media communication strategies to meet various organizational/business goals, such as product/service sales, campaigns, reputation management, and crisis management.

Participants will be exposed to current ethical and legal issues in social media, such as misinformation, sponsored social media content, and artificial intelligence/ algorithm use.
Social Media Branding Course Description Social media platforms play an essential role in how organizations communicate with their audiences.
This course will introduce strategies for developing an effective social media branding campaign.
You will learn how to set measurable campaign goals and use storytelling techniques to create diverse and accessible content for appropriate social media campaigns.
Modes of Creative Content Creation Course Description This course offers an introduction to the modern content creation landscape, with specific focus on best practices for social media applications.
Students will engage in crafting creative briefs, pre-production, production and post production while creating content for campaigns of their own.

Report from Faculty Senate Executive Committee February 23, 2023 Senate Terms Rationale: Senators who have been productive members of Standing Committees and who wish to continue to serve, should not be obligated to a one year lapse. Allowing for consecutive terms may foster continuation of the Committees goals and create much-needed institutional memory. Motion: Adjust all term limits to allow for two consecutive terms in the Senate without a mandatory one year lapse. Appendix C of the University Manual, By-laws of the Faculty Senate Section 2, Election of Senators Existing Language: 2.7 A senator whose three-year term expires may not be re-elected until the lapse of one year, except that a senator who has not served for two or more consecutive semesters of a three-year term on account of an officially sanctioned leave (sabbatical, medical, and the like) shall be eligible for re-election without a one-year hiatus. #01-02–29 Proposal: 2.7 A senator may be re-elected to serve a second consecutive term, after which they whose three-year term expires may not be re-elected until the lapse of one year, except that a senator who has not served for two or more consecutive semesters of a three-year term on account of an officially sanctioned leave (sabbatical, medical, and the like) shall be eligible for re-election without a one-year hiatus. #01-02–29
